Sunday Skate Club ft. Sissies of Mercy | Club Flush: Sidestreets (skate)

A love letter to Sunday Skate Club 🫶

Every Sunday from 8–12am, the rink becomes more than a skate session. It’s a weekly ritual where local club kids, industry folks, and NYC’s DJs get their flowers — and skate heads and music heads move in the same orbit.

Here you see the true versatility of a DJ. That epic artist you loved at 5am now accepts the challenge of an all-skate set around a groovy 100bpm — R&B, disco, and other unexpected jams. It’s a rare chance to hear their non-unz unz selections like R&B, disco, you name it. From thudding foggy sweaty beats the morning before (well, it may have still been your ‘night’) to idyllic skating in a psychedelic rink with jams that make you smile big. You start with a few laps, feeling out the floor, the room fills, the rhythm builds, and before long, you’re moving without thinking — just you, the music, and the night.

Then you notice friends slipping into the bathrooms… only it’s Club Flush, pulling the off-wheels crowd into something sweatier, louder, a little unhinged. Red-lit and hazy, fog stretching the room so it feels bigger than it is. An 18” sub shakes the floor, a hidden 21” built straight into the booth hits your chest. There are no grimy stalls, no smells (thanks all!) just a fully enclosed, immersive room. A few minutes in, and you forget you’re even standing in a bathroom. You might walk in for a second and stay for half a set. You might discover your new favorite DJ. You might skate, then dance, then skate again. That’s the point.

Every week is a different crew, a different sound, a different pocket of the city’s underground stepping forward. Sunday Skate Club is about unified movement — wheels, feet, bass, community. When these scenes overlap, the energy multiplies, and the night becomes something bigger than the sum of its parts.

See you every Sunday at 8.

Sunday Skate Club ft. DJ Dream, Conrad Dirty Finger | Club Flush: Zariya & Mantle (skate)

A love letter to Sunday Skate Club 🫶

Every Sunday from 8–12am, the rink becomes more than a skate session. It’s a weekly ritual where local club kids, industry folks, and NYC’s DJs get their flowers — and skate heads and music heads move in the same orbit.

Here you see the true versatility of a DJ. That epic artist you loved at 5am now accepts the challenge of an all-skate set around a groovy 100bpm — R&B, disco, and other unexpected jams. It’s a rare chance to hear their non-unz unz selections like R&B, disco, you name it. From thudding foggy sweaty beats the morning before (well, it may have still been your ‘night’) to idyllic skating in a psychedelic rink with jams that make you smile big. You start with a few laps, feeling out the floor, the room fills, the rhythm builds, and before long, you’re moving without thinking — just you, the music, and the night.

Then you notice friends slipping into the bathrooms… only it’s Club Flush, pulling the off-wheels crowd into something sweatier, louder, a little unhinged. Red-lit and hazy, fog stretching the room so it feels bigger than it is. An 18” sub shakes the floor, a hidden 21” built straight into the booth hits your chest. There are no grimy stalls, no smells (thanks all!) just a fully enclosed, immersive room. A few minutes in, and you forget you’re even standing in a bathroom. You might walk in for a second and stay for half a set. You might discover your new favorite DJ. You might skate, then dance, then skate again. That’s the point.

Every week is a different crew, a different sound, a different pocket of the city’s underground stepping forward. Sunday Skate Club is about unified movement — wheels, feet, bass, community. When these scenes overlap, the energy multiplies, and the night becomes something bigger than the sum of its parts.

*Heavy Debt* is the debut solo album from Shane Butler, best known for work with his projects Olden Yolk and Quilt. Marking his first release since Olden Yolk’s 2019 album Living Theatre, the album refines the art-leaning folk of Butler’s past projects into a sharp, singular vision. While retaining many of the neo-psychedelic qualities of Butler's past work, Heavy Debt occupies a more grounded terrain—establishing a firm sonic and lyrical footing in a candid world entirely his own. Recorded in New York during the winter of 2025 alongside producer and multi instrumentalist Jon Nellen, the album pairs rapidly picked guitars and effected woodwinds (played by Isaiah Barr of experimental jazz troupe Onyx Collective) with rich, varied percussion. These calibrated arrangements anchor Butler’s playful lyrics, weaving semi-autobiographical stories about the vagaries of modern life with a plainspoken clarity and a dreamlike fiction.

The group stretches the sonic possibilities of their instruments while exploring long-form, texture-driven minimalism and time-based improvisation.

**Emma Ruth Rundle** made a conscious choice to reach towards making a hopeful record for the follow up to 2021’s *Engine of Hell*. Where outside forces tempted her to turn inwards, towards isolation and hopelessness, she instead reached outwards to create a record that acknowledges pain, but offers both community and resilience in response. Although *These Killing Times* possesses a spirit of defiance, it retains the tenderness and vulnerability that saw her earlier work resonate with so many listeners.

*These Killing Times* is electrifying, emotional, and charged with feminine rage; it is a reactive anthology, bristling, full of life and full of resistance - forged by and for community. It asks many questions - of the roles we play as individuals, or as artists - and closes with this one: what will we live for beyond the valley of the shadow of the fear of all men? A question with no definitive answer as yet, but one that is being asked with increasing urgency - here on this record, and beyond.

**Cinder Well** is the musical project of Los Angeles–based songwriter, composer, and multi-instrumentalist Amelia Baker. Cinder Well extracts dark, rich and tender compositions which nod to, but also stray from traditional musical languages.

Succinct pauses, surreal frequencies and effects, breakneck pace and sharply hurled vocals characterize the band’s aesthetic, which seems as though it is rooted in a sort of nasty-sound-meets-highbrow-message ethos. Fueled by the onslaught of society’s insanity and driven mad by tinnitus, Justin Pearson (The Locust, Dead Cross), Brian Amalfitano, Scott Osment (Glassing, Planet B), and Collin Smith approach music as an opportunity to confront our collective sicknesses.

The band initially released their debut EP, Contemporary Sickness, via Three One G in 2019. Having had time to stew in the cesspool of two years of pandemic, and mutating into its newest variant, their debut longplayer, Productive Disruption, dropped in 2022, ventured deeper into the abyss. 2025’s sophomore album, We Demand a Permanent State of Happiness was released on Southern Lord September 2025. Since then the band have been touring regularly across North America and Europe, including an appearance at Roskilde Festival. **Emma Ruth Rundle** made a conscious choice to reach towards making a hopeful record for the follow up to 2021’s *Engine of Hell*. Where outside forces tempted her to turn inwards, towards isolation and hopelessness, she instead reached outwards to create a record that acknowledges pain, but offers both community and resilience in response. Although *These Killing Times* possesses a spirit of defiance, it retains the tenderness and vulnerability that saw her earlier work resonate with so many listeners.

*These Killing Times* is electrifying, emotional, and charged with feminine rage; it is a reactive anthology, bristling, full of life and full of resistance - forged by and for community. It asks many questions - of the roles we play as individuals, or as artists - and closes with this one: what will we live for beyond the valley of the shadow of the fear of all men? A question with no definitive answer as yet, but one that is being asked with increasing urgency - here on this record, and beyond.
